props.title: And Now for Something Completely Different
props.initialSlug: A wacky sketch comedy feast from Monty Python

sections.content: And Now for Something Completely Different (1971) marks Monty Python's explosive leap from TV to cinema, compiling and re-filming their best Flying Circus sketches with cinematic flair. The film's rapid-fire absurdity established a new comedy language that influenced everything from Airplane! (1980) to The Naked Gun (1988). The Dead Parrot sketch, Lumberjack Song, and Upper Class Twit of the Year competition showcase the group's brilliant mix of intellectual wit and slapstick lunacy. Director Ian MacNaughton's decision to shoot fresh versions rather than simply compile TV clips gave the material new energy and visual polish.

sections.content: The film's influence on sketch comedy cinema cannot be overstated. Kentucky Fried Movie (1977) and Amazon Women on the Moon (1987) adopted its rapid-fire format, while UHF (1989) channeled its surreal parody style. The Pythons proved sketch comedy could work cinematically by embracing the absurd and maintaining relentless pacing. Their sophisticated silly-to-smart ratio became the template for modern comedy anthologies.

The innovative animation segments by Terry Gilliam created a distinctive visual style that would influence music videos and commercial advertising for decades. His cut-out technique and stream-of-consciousness imagery can be seen echoed in works like Pink Floyd: The Wall (1982) and modern Adult Swim programming. The film's fearless mixing of highbrow references and lowbrow humor created a new comedy framework that directors like Edgar Wright and Taika Waititi still draw from today. sections.content: The DNA of And Now for Something Completely Different appears throughout contemporary comedy. Wet Hot American Summer (2001) and They Came Together (2014) employ similar genre deconstruction techniques. The absurdist transitions and non sequiturs influenced shows like Mr. Show (1995) and sketch groups like The State. Even Scott Pilgrim vs. the World (2010) owes a debt to Python's fearless genre-bending and fourth-wall breaks.
